collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager pours out a work problem to a friend who loves solving problems: the friend gives advice, or just listens.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) sits down next to (friend) and starts talking about a problem with (subject.his/her) work crew: who is doing what, who isn't, how annoying it all is. (friend), who is very good at solving problems, opens (friend.his/her) mouth to start solving.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Well, what you should do is..." says (friend). (subject) holds up a hand. "I don't want advice," (subject.he/she) says. "I just want to say it out loud to someone." (friend) closes (friend.his/her) mouth. It is very hard. (friend.He/she) listens. (subject) talks for a long time, then stands up, stretches and says, "Thank you. That helped." Nothing has been decided. Both of them feel strangely good about it.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) bites (friend.his/her) tongue and listens. Nods. Says "Hmm" in the right places. When (subject) finally stops, (friend) says, "That sounds annoying." "It IS annoying," says (subject), clearly relieved. That's all. (subject) goes back to the crew. Nothing about the crew has changed. (subject) has.
